statement: In the laboratory studies of repeated MDMA dosing, the strain on the circulation followed the blood concentration even where the wanted effects did not. After a second 100 mg dose 24 hours after the first, 8 of 9 men crossed 140 mm Hg systolic against 6 of 9 after the first dose, with episodes lasting on average 1.4 hours (range 0.5-3) against 1 hour (0.5-2), and the only two episodes of sinus tachycardia above 100 beats a minute both followed the second dose (Farre et al., 2004). With 50 mg followed by 100 mg two hours later, all 10 men exceeded 140/90 mm Hg, and blood pressure, temperature and pupil diameter rose with the added dose while heart rate and the wanted effects did not (Peiro et al., 2013). In the registered booster study, blood pressure, heart rate and temperature were prolonged but not raised at the peak, and no participant exceeded 180 mm Hg systolic or 40 degrees Celsius (Humbert-Droz et al., 2026). This matters because taking more to make up for an effect that no longer grows adds the cardiovascular load without the sought-after effect. The numbers are small (9, 10 and 23 healthy screened people, two studies in men only), the doses are 50 to 180 mg of pure MDMA taken seated in a quiet room, and nobody has tested the hotter, more crowded, more active settings or the larger amounts described in surveys.
plain: When people take a second dose, the drug level in the blood rises more than the extra dose alone explains, and the strain on the heart and circulation goes up with it, even though the good feelings do not get stronger. In one study, 8 of 9 men went above a raised blood-pressure line after the second dose, against 6 of 9 after the first, and the two cases of a racing heart both came after the second dose. In another, all ten men went above that line. Nobody has tested this in a hot, crowded room or with the larger amounts people describe in surveys.
population: Healthy adults with previous recreational MDMA experience in laboratory studies (9 men; 10 men; 23 people of whom 11 were women), screened to exclude cardiovascular, other medical and psychiatric illness
exposure: A second dose of MDMA taken 2 or 24 hours after the first (study conditions: 100 mg then 100 mg 24 hours apart; 50 mg then 100 mg 2 hours apart; 120 mg then 60 mg 2 hours apart), taken seated in a quiet laboratory
comparator: The same people after a single dose or placebo, and their own first dose
outcome: Blood pressure and heart rate, the number of people crossing clinical thresholds, body temperature, and reported adverse effects
magnitude: Twenty-four-hour interval: isolated systolic hypertension (above 140 mm Hg) in 6 of 9 men after the first dose and 8 of 9 after the second; mean episode duration 1 h (range 0.5-2) against 1.4 h (range 0.5-3); two men met criteria for sinus tachycardia (above 100 beats/min), both after the second dose, lasting 15-30 minutes; peak systolic rise 34 mm Hg against 25 and diastolic 20 against 10 (Farre et al., 2004). Two-hour interval: all 10 men exceeded 140/90 mm Hg; systolic area under the curve 72.96 (SD 22.12) against 49.35 (SD 24.28), p=0.029, and diastolic 46.82 (SD 27.82) against 18.81 (SD 21.09), p=0.015, with heart rate unchanged (Peiro et al., 2013). Booster study: autonomic effects prolonged without higher maxima, no systolic pressure above 180 mm Hg and no temperature above 40 degrees Celsius; acute complaint scores 22 (SD 15) with the booster against 20 (SD 13) with the single dose, not significantly different, with vomiting in 3 of 23 (13%) against 2 (9%) (Humbert-Droz et al., 2026).

evidence.locator: Results > Pharmacological effects, the paragraph beginning 'In reference to physiological parameters' (right column)
evidence.extracted: Criteria for isolated systolic hypertension (above 140 mm Hg) were met by 6 of 9 men after the first 100 mg dose and by 8 of 9 after the second dose 24 hours later, with episodes lasting a mean of 1 h (range 0.5-2) and 1.4 h (range 0.5-3); two men met criteria for sinus tachycardia (above 100 beats/min), both after the second dose, lasting 15-30 minutes. Peak rises were 34 mm Hg systolic and 20 diastolic after the second dose against 25 and 10 after the first.

evidence.locator: Table 1, SBP and DBP rows (p. 887); Results > Physiological measures, 1st paragraph (p. 888)
evidence.extracted: With 50 mg two hours before 100 mg, every one of the ten men exceeded 140/90 mm Hg; the systolic area under the curve over the 2-6 hour window was 72.96 (SD 22.12) against 49.35 (SD 24.28) for 100 mg alone (p=0.029) and the diastolic 46.82 (SD 27.82) against 18.81 (SD 21.09) (p=0.015), while heart rate did not differ in peak or area under the curve.

evidence.locator: Results > Autonomic effects; Table 2, List of complaints rows; Results > Acute and subacute adverse effects, 1st and 3rd paragraphs
evidence.extracted: With a 60 mg booster two hours after 120 mg, blood pressure, heart rate, rate-pressure product and temperature lasted longer than with the single dose but did not reach higher maxima, and no participant exceeded 180 mm Hg systolic or 40 degrees Celsius. Acute complaint scores did not differ significantly between booster and single dose (22, SD 15, against 20, SD 13), although two of 25 participants, both women receiving the booster as their first MDMA experience, left the study after headache and nausea followed by weeks of anxiety and restlessness, and are excluded from that comparison.

evidence.locator: Discussion, the paragraph beginning 'The changes seen in the concentrations between first and second doses'
evidence.extracted: The authors note that acute MDMA toxicity has been linked to high plasma concentrations and doses, that cardiovascular complications were more frequent after the second dose in their study, and that with further doses the contribution of each previous dose would grow because MDMA inhibits its own metabolism; they present this as speculation about what would happen beyond two doses, which was not tested.

risk_of_bias.note: Randomized or counterbalanced double-blind crossovers with instrument-measured blood pressure, heart rate and temperature, which the broken blinding affects little; but the threshold counts were not pre-specified outcomes and the studies tested many measures without correction.

inconsistency.note: Three studies agree that the circulatory load tracks concentration; they differ in whether the peak or only the duration rises, which the claim states.

indirectness.note: The claim is worded for the doses, settings and people studied, and says that hotter, more crowded settings and larger amounts are untested.

imprecision.note: The threshold counts are 6 of 9 against 8 of 9 and 10 of 10, with no intervals; a difference of two people in nine cannot support a quantitative statement about how much redosing raises the risk.

grade.reasoning: Placebo-controlled within-person laboratory studies start high (METHODS 6.3). Risk of bias -1: the measures that matter here are instrument-recorded, but the threshold counts are post-hoc descriptions rather than pre-specified outcomes. Imprecision -2: the counts come from 9 and 10 people and no intervals are given, so the claim can report what happened in those men but not a risk. Certainty very-low. The claim is deliberately worded as what was measured in these sessions, with the inference that redosing adds circulatory load without added wanted effect stated as the combination of two measured findings, not as a tested outcome.

verification.flag_note: Section 6 claim drawn from studies designed to measure pharmacology rather than harm; the senior author may prefer it merged into the acute-risks claim on cardiovascular effects once that exists.

changelog.change: New draft claim from three full texts read in this round (Farre et al., 2004; Peiro et al., 2013; Humbert-Droz et al., 2026). Written because the evidence for tolerance to the wanted effects of a second dose comes with measured cardiovascular changes in the same sessions, which is what a reader deciding whether to take another dose needs; section 6 of the monograph template covers acute risks. Anchors ai-located by the first reader and not yet checked.
